bank.y.name: Y — result
bank.d1.name: Δ₁ — first difference
bank.d2.name: Δ₂ — second difference
note_html: Pedagogical figure-wheel model of decimal carry inside one Difference Engine–style difference cycle — not a full No. 2 reconstruction. Analytical Engine (store/mill/cards): see the Fourmilab lab on this chapter. Door-outs: Science Museum, Computer History Museum, Plan 28.
guide.ready.body: Press Step. One finite-difference cycle: add Δ₁ into Y, then add Δ₂ into Δ₁. When a wheel rolls past 9, watch the arm catch the next column.
guide.ready.hint: Start at x=3 (Y=9, Δ₁=7, Δ₂=2) so the first Step produces a carry into tens.
guide.carry.body: {label}: wheel rolled past 9→{digit}. A tooth catches the next column toward {dest}.
guide.carry.hint: That catch is the physical event Babbage’s columns enforced.
log.overflow: {label} overflow past column width — widen in a real engine.
guide.step1.body: First half of the difference cycle: add the first-difference column into the result.
guide.step1.hint: Watch for a rollover past 9 on Y.
guide.step2.body: Second half: the constant second difference advances Δ₁ for the next cycle.
guide.step2.hint: Carry can happen here too on later steps.
guide.settle.body.ok: Cycle done. Y is now {y} (= {x}²). Step again to continue the table.
guide.settle.body.bad: Cycle done. Y is now {y}. Step again to continue the table.
guide.settle.hint: Reset (carry ready) jumps back to Y=9 so the carry is obvious on the first Step.
log.reset: Reset at x=3 (Y=9, Δ₁=7, Δ₂=2). First Step should carry on Y: 9+7 → 16.
log.classic: Classic start x=0 (Y=0, Δ₁=1, Δ₂=2). Carry appears when Y reaches 9+7.
guide.classic.body: Same engine, blank table. Step repeatedly; carry shows once Y approaches 9.
guide.classic.hint: Or use Reset (carry ready) to jump straight to the tooth-catch moment.
